summary: Builds skinned surfaces over faces or surface boundary curves, supporting linear, bilinear, swept, triangular, square, and multiple-boundary cases.

key_params.name: skinops
key_params.note: Skin all primitives, groups, or skipped sets

key_params.name: inc
key_params.note: N value for grouped or skipped skinning

key_params.name: polys
key_params.note: Convert mesh surface output to polygons

common_gotchas: Parametric direction must match across cross-sections or surfaces can twist or flip.
Preserve Shape is disabled for bilinear skinning and may look unintuitive with coincident or very close CVs.
V Wrap and V Order are ignored in bilinear cases, and V Order is also irrelevant for all-polygon or all-mesh inputs.
Use Bridge SOP when tangency control is more important than broad skin construction.
key_concepts: Skin SOP builds surfaces across faces or surface boundary curves.
Inputs should contain only faces or only surfaces, though the individual face/surface types can differ.
One input performs linear skinning across cross-sections; a second input enables bilinear cross-skinning.
Sort SOP or Primitive SOP can correct ordering and parametric direction when twists or flips appear.
